info.description:
PagerDuty REST API provides access to on-call management, incident response, service catalog, escalation policies, and schedules in the PagerDuty platform.

Authentication: API key in Authorization header — generate a REST API key from PagerDuty under My Profile → User Settings → API Access or as a general access API key under Integrations → API Access Keys. Pass as Authorization: Token token=<api_key>.

Source: https://developer.pagerduty.com/api-reference/
info.title: PagerDuty
info.x-itential-curated: Trimmed to 88 of 425 upstream operations covering common CRUD for automation: incidents, services and their integration keys, escalation policies, schedules (including overrides and on-call schedule membership), on-call queries, teams, users (including contact methods and notification rules), maintenance windows, business services, change events, priorities, and tags. See the repo README for the full scope and the full spec.

tags.name: Abilities
tags.description:
This describes your account's abilities by feature name. For example `"teams"`.
An ability may be available to your account based on things like your pricing plan or account state.

tags.name: Add-ons
tags.description: Developers can write their own functionality to insert into PagerDuty's UI.

tags.name: Alert Grouping Settings
tags.description: Alert Grouping Settings allow you to configure how alerts in services are grouped together into incidents.

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description: Provides enriched incident data.

tags.name: Audit
tags.description: Provides audit record data.

tags.name: Automation Actions
tags.description: Automation Actions invoke jobs that are staged in Runbook Automation or Process Automation.

tags.name: Paused Incident Reports
tags.description: Provides paused Incident reporting data on services and accounts that have paused Alerts.

tags.name: Business Services
tags.description: Business services model capabilities that span multiple technical services and that may be owned by several different teams.

tags.name: Change Events
tags.description: Change Events enable you to send informational events about recent changes such as code deploys and system config changes from any system that can make an outbound HTTP connection. These events do not create incidents and do not send notifications; they are shown in context with incidents on the same PagerDuty service.

tags.name: Escalation Policies
tags.description: Escalation policies define which user should be alerted at which time.

tags.name: Event Orchestrations
tags.description: Event Orchestrations allow you to route events to an endpoint and create collections of Event Orchestrations, which define sets of actions to take based on event content.

tags.name: Extension Schemas
tags.description: A PagerDuty extension vendor represents a specific type of outbound extension such as Generic Webhook, Slack, ServiceNow.

tags.name: Extensions
tags.description: Extensions are representations of Extension Schema objects that are attached to Services.

tags.name: Incidents
tags.description: An incident represents a problem or an issue that needs to be addressed and resolved. Incidents trigger on a service, which prompts notifications to go out to on-call responders per the service's escalation policy.

tags.name: Incident Custom Fields
tags.description: Custom fields allow you to enrich PagerDuty incidents with critical and helpful metadata throughout the incident lifecycle.

tags.name: Incident Types
tags.description: Incident Types are a feature which will allow customers to categorize incidents, such as a security incident, a major incident, or a fraud incident.

tags.name: Incident Workflows
tags.description: An Incident Workflow is a sequence of configurable Steps and associated Triggers that can execute automated Actions for a given Incident.

tags.name: IP Allow Lists
tags.description:
Manage account-level IP Allow Lists that restrict access to your PagerDuty subdomain to a configured set of IPv4 CIDR ranges. Enforcement currently applies to web and mobile application traffic.


<!-- theme: warning -->

> ### Early Access
> This API is in Early Access and may change at any time. You must pass the `X-EARLY-ACCESS: ip-allow-lists` header on every request, and your account must be enrolled in the IP Allow Lists Early Access program. Contact your PagerDuty account team to request access.

tags.name: Licenses
tags.description: Licenses are allocated to Users to allow for per-User access to PagerDuty functionality within an Account.

tags.name: Log Entries
tags.description: A log of all the events that happen to an Incident, and these are exposed as Log Entries.

tags.name: Maintenance Windows
tags.description: A Maintenance Window is used to temporarily disable one or more Services for a set period of time.

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: A Notification is created when an Incident is triggered or escalated.

tags.name: OAuth Delegations
tags.description: An OAuth Delegation represents a delegation of a User's permissions to an OAuth Client, allowing the client to impersonate the user when making API requests.

tags.name: On-Calls
tags.description: An on-call represents a contiguous unit of time for which a User will be on call for a given Escalation Policy and Escalation Rules

tags.name: Priorities
tags.description: A priority is a label representing the importance and impact of an incident. This feature is only available on Standard and Enterprise plans.

tags.name: Rulesets
tags.description: Rulesets allow you to route events to an endpoint and create collections of Event Rules, which define sets of actions to take based on event content.

tags.name: Schedules
tags.description: A Schedule determines the time periods that users are On-Call.

tags.name: Schedules_v3
tags.description:
Shift-Based Schedules API. Creates and manages on-call schedules using a rotation and event model.


<!-- theme: info -->

> **Important note:** Shift-based schedules use the V3 API and are not compatible with V2 automations. **To create automations for Shift-Based Schedules, you need to:**
>
> 1. **Update your automations** to use the V3 API for all new shift-based schedules
> 2. **Keep the V2 endpoint** for your existing schedules
>
> An upgrade tool for existing schedules is coming soon; your legacy schedules will keep working in the meantime. [Learn more](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/shift-based-schedules-api-upgrade-examples).

tags.name: Service Dependencies
tags.description: Services are categorized into technical and business services. Dependencies can be created via any combination of these services.

tags.name: Services
tags.description: A Service may represent an application, component, or team you wish to open incidents against.

tags.name: Service Custom Fields
tags.description: Custom fields allow you to enrich PagerDuty services with critical and helpful metadata throughout the Service lifecycle.

tags.name: SRE Agent
tags.description: The SRE Agent uses AI to help manage and resolve incidents. Memories are knowledge learned by the SRE Agent from past incidents and conversations.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
A webhook is a way to receive events that occur on the PagerDuty platform via an HTTP POST request.
V3 webhooks are set up by creating a webhook subscription.

tags.name: Standards
tags.description: Standards help provide a clear understanding of what a good service configuration looks like, allowing to share and enforce organization guidelines across services to ensure adherence to best practices.

tags.name: Status Dashboards
tags.description: Status Dashboards represent user-defined views for the Status Dashboard product that are limited to specific Business Services rather than the whole set of top-level Business Services (those with no dependent Services).

tags.name: Status Pages
tags.description: Status Pages can be public or private read-only pages, that display the status of some predefined set of services, to be shared with customers or internal stakeholders.

tags.name: Tags
tags.description: A Tag is applied to Escalation Policies, Teams or Users and can be used to filter them.

tags.name: Teams
tags.description: A team is a collection of Users and Escalation Policies that represent a group of people within an organization.

tags.name: Templates
tags.description: Templates is a new feature which will allow customers to create message templates to be leveraged by (but not limited to) status updates. The API will be secured to customers with the status updates entitlements.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: Users are members of a PagerDuty account that have the ability to interact with Incidents and other data on the account.

tags.name: Vendors
tags.description: A PagerDuty Vendor represents a specific type of integration. AWS Cloudwatch, Splunk, Datadog are all examples of vendors

tags.name: Workflow Integrations
tags.description: Workflow Integrations are a way to connect PagerDuty to other tools and services.

The current state of the Service. Valid statuses are:


- `active`: The service is enabled and has no open incidents. This is the only status a service can be created with.
- `warning`: The service is enabled and has one or more acknowledged incidents.
- `critical`: The service is enabled and has one or more triggered incidents.

post.description:
Assign existing or new tags.

A Tag is applied to Escalation Policies, Teams or Users and can be used to filter them.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#tags)

Scoped OAuth requires: `tags.write`

schema.description: Tags to add to or remove from the entity.

add.description:
Array of tags and/or tag references to add to the entity.
For elements with type `tag_reference`, the tag with the corresponding `id` is added to the entity.
For elements with type `tag`, if there is an existing tag with the given
label that tag is added to the entity. If there is no existing tag with that label and the user has permission
to create tags, a new tag is created with that label and assigned to the entity.

label.description: The label of the tag. Should be used when type is "tag".

id.description: The id of the tag. Should be used when type is "tag_reference".

remove.description: Array of tag references to remove from the entity.

200.description: The tags were added and/or removed.

get.description:

A Tag is applied to Escalation Policies, Teams or Users and can be used to filter them.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#tags)

Scoped OAuth requires: `tags.read`
